title: Stage 5 identity role and key change audit record v1
description: Normalized, signed audit event for changes to privileged governance-role grants or human signing-key bindings.
$comment: The identity source or its pinned adapter retains these records in an immutable, ordered history. approval.approved_change_sha256 is SHA-256(JCS({schema,source_id,role_change_id,sequence,previous_record_sha256,environment_id,log_id,action,target_subject_id,role,signing_key_id,key_fingerprint_sha256,actor_subject_id,approver_subject_id,approval_policy_id,approval_policy_sha256,approval_policy_revision,effective_at_utc,reason_code})); the approver signs that exact intent before the source commits it. The approval signature covers JCS({schema,approval_id,approval_policy_id,approval_policy_sha256,approval_policy_revision,approver_subject_id,approver_signing_key_id,approved_change_sha256,signed_at_utc,signature_profile}) using ed25519-jcs-identity-role-change-approval-v1. record_sha256 is SHA-256(JCS(the event with record_sha256 and signature omitted)). The source signature covers JCS({schema, source_id, record_sha256, sequence, previous_record_sha256, recorded_at_utc, signature_profile, signature_key_id}) using ed25519-jcs-identity-role-change-v1. Semantic verification must recompute the approved intent digest, resolve the exact policy digest and revision from verifier-pinned configuration history, verify the approver signature and key-to-subject binding at signed_at_utc, require approval.approver_subject_id == approver_subject_id, require actor_subject_id != approver_subject_id, require target subject distinct from both administrators, and check chain/head freshness and temporal ordering. Grants and key bindings cannot be backdated before recorded_at_utc; a backdated revocation/key revocation must trigger re-evaluation of decisions in the affected interval. If identity-administrator compromise is in scope, an independent witness or equivalent tamper-evident checkpoint must protect the role-change history head.
